title: Injury Q&A #4
summary: Fourth injury Q&A covering forearm and elbow pain, muscle imbalances, chest and upper back strains, SI joint pain, hip tightness, low bar thumb pain, shoulder pain from benching, deep squats and piriformis issues. Recurring themes: surprise motion causes injuries, rehab instead of just resting, and fix pressing and hinging technique.
claims: Forearm pain on curls, between forearm and biceps, is usually more painful than dangerous; pain inside the elbow at the tendon insertion is a different story
Forearm pain often comes from constant gripping tension; train hand opening with elastic bands
For curl-related forearm pain, lower the load and do more reps; if it goes away, alternate heavier low-rep work with lighter volume
An overdeveloped muscle is not the problem, an underdeveloped one is; big quads prevent knee pain, and growing his quads, not glutes or hamstrings, cured his chronic patellar tendinitis
An aggravated tendon is doing too much work; strengthen the surrounding muscles so they take over
Keep feeding the big muscle and train its partner more rather than holding it back: heavy pressing calls for lots of rear delt work
Balance knee flexion and hip hinge with a slight bias toward hinges, and pull more than you press (not necessarily 2:1) because the upper back handles more volume
Pec strains are extremely painful but usually heal on their own; pain when breathing or bracing points to a rib, intercostal or upper back problem instead
Upper back pain is often just an aggravated nerve out of position
For an upper back injury, take two days off, then avoid painful exercises; if every movement hurts, see a doctor
Returning from an upper back injury: squats and good mornings come back first, then vertical then horizontal presses, then deadlifts, and rows last
Never lift heavy without warming up and do not grind ugly reps; it is useless
Never do pullovers for fewer than 6 reps; they put the shoulders in a stressful position and hurt people lacking mobility
His cheap elastic elbow wraps do nothing for performance but keep the elbow warm and work as a placebo, so he wears them
Music takes your mind off pain; like a child who only cries when given permission, do not let your body make you feel pain at every pop
Hand opening with elastic bands, 3x a week then daily, makes a massive difference for wrist, finger and hand pain
Most so-called back pain is actually SI joint pain; disc herniation is rare. The SI joint needs recovery, so do not hit it every session
A burning bar of fire in the lower back after deadlifts or squats is not a pump but an abused tendon from bad programming and form; lift with your legs and use the lower back as a bridge
Reject programs with squats and deadlifts on the same day or squats three times a week
Upper back injuries are sharp and random; you can pop something just by sneezing
Many injuries come from surprise: unexpected motion and timing, such as over-exaggerating the lockout on RDLs. Keep the shoulders still
Toe touching is a poor hamstring or hip gauge because of proportions; your natural squat stance shows your hip structure, and a seated figure-four knee press reveals tight hips
Tight hips limit squat depth and make the hips shoot up on deadlifts; build mobility with some stretches, then keep lifting
The limited range on preacher curls is the correct range; do not overextend at the bottom of curls
Squeezing the bar as hard as possible is mostly a psychological myth and can shift the bar into the center of the palm, taxing the forearms; relax your grip
Low bar squats load the hand and thumb; instead of wrapping the bar, go thumbless and press up from slightly underneath. He did low bar this way because of wrist pain
Elbow clicking without pain after tendinitis is not concerning; the tendon just has more room. Wrap it if it bothers you
Sleeves and wraps mainly help injury prevention psychologically, not performance, and are still worth buying
Most shoulder or AC joint pain comes from the bench: add an arch, slow the negative, fix the bar path and tuck the elbows, then rebuild from light weight using close or neutral grip meanwhile
Wide grips on bench and overhead press put the shoulder in internal rotation; use a narrower grip on the press
Resting an injury without rehab leaves it in perpetual trauma, like walking away from a broken glass without cleaning it
The most dangerous point of a lift is the reversal from negative to positive, where posture shifts at maximum speed
One day of mediocre form is enough to get injured; once hurt, good rehab fixes it, not good technique
For SI joint pain, dead hangs and leg raises traction the lower back; add dead hangs at the end of pull days and deload hinges slightly to relearn pain-free lifting
Pain is learned; if you expect pain on a lift you will feel it, so rebuild a relationship with the lift divorced from pain
Deep squats are fine and good for the knees when knee travel is controlled; the danger is knees shooting forward or caving out of the hole on the knee's elasticity
Squat as deep as you can without back or knee pain; ass to grass depends on your build
For piriformis or high hamstring nerve pain, do stretch-focused hinges (RDLs, hyperextensions), leg curls and careful Nordic curls, since squats and deadlifts only tense the area
Wrist pain after EZ curls: try an engaged wrist position, wrist wraps, elastic band work, and superset long head triceps work with the curls
Narrow commercial benches leave a shoulder blade unsupported during dumbbell presses, forcing the upper back to compensate and get injured
Mental illness and everyday stress impair recovery and raise injury rates
An unrehabbed injury spreads like a black hole: a knee problem can grow into hip and hamstring problems
Coming back after a two-month break at the same weight leaves knees sore; ramp back up gradually

A fragile hip structure (strong legs but weak glutes, lower back and hips): build it with hip thrusts, back hyperextensions and bridges, and squat lighter, e.g. two plates instead of three, for high volume and perfect execution
exercises: open the hand against the band, 3x/wk then daily
fixes forearm, wrist, finger and hand pain from constant gripping
shoulders at risk in stretched position
limited range is the correct range
thumbless, press up from under the bar
less load on thumb and wrist
tractions lower back and SI joint
relieves piriformis and high hamstring tension
builds lower back and hip structure
